summary.name: Internet forum
summary.one_liner: An Internet forum (message board) is an online discussion platform where users post messages in threads that are at least temporarily archived, described here as a general concept rather than a specific product.
use_cases: hosting community discussions on a topic
running a support or Q&A board
summary.what_it_does: The page is a Wikipedia article describing internet forums as hierarchical, tree-like discussion platforms made of categories, sub-forums, and threads. It covers history from early BBS and Usenet systems through early web forums, and notes that forum software packages are written in languages such as PHP, Perl, Java, and ASP. It also describes common features such as user groups, moderator and admin roles, private messages, attachments, BBCode, emoticons, polls, and ignore lists. Much of the text discusses the forum concept and its social dynamics rather than one tool.
notable: Threads, sub-forums, and categories form a tree-like structure
Describes BBCode, tripcodes, and capcodes as forum-specific conventions
Covers moderator and administrator roles and user groups
caveats: The page is an encyclopedia overview, not a downloadable product, so no specific software is named as available for use
Some claims are marked as needing citations
